note: Voice direction for the build-time speech pipeline (spec 20.4/20.6/62). Every speaker in SPEAKER_IDS must have an entry. Edited by hand; consumed by scripts/vo/generate_vo.py and validated by src/game/dialogue/voiceSchema.ts.

output.note: MP3 rather than Ogg/Opus deliberately. Opus is smaller at this bitrate, but Safari and iOS cannot decode Ogg through AudioContext.decodeAudioData, and spec 21 requires the whole campaign to be completable on iOS. Mono 48 kbit/s at 24 kHz is transparent enough for speech and keeps a 380-line campaign near 11 MB. Change `container` to `ogg` (codec libopus) for an Android/desktop-only build.

loudness.note: EBU R128 via ffmpeg two-pass loudnorm (spec 74). -19 LUFS sits under the music and ambience beds while staying intelligible on a phone speaker. Per-character `loudnessOffsetDb` shifts this target rather than the raw gain, so a tired delivery stays quieter than a raised voice after normalisation instead of being flattened to the same level.

silence.note: Edge's service pads a variable head and tail; untrimmed, a one-word line like Mara's "Half." arrives with a third of a second of nothing in front of it and reads as a missed cue. `interruptedTailMs` is 0 for a line whose text ends in an em dash, so a cut-off line stops dead where the interrupt lands.

textTransforms.note: The synthesiser reads punctuation, not stage direction. A leading em dash marks a cut-in and is silent; a trailing one marks being cut off. An interior em dash is a breath, and a comma is the only pause edge-tts will honour. See the pause-strategy note on the backend below.

pronunciations.note: Global substitutions applied before synthesis; per-character maps override them. Kept deliberately near-empty. Every entry is a place the spoken line can drift from the subtitle, and the subtitle is the authored text, so a substitution has to earn its place. Verified as NOT needing entries: initial identifiers such as "Cluster B" and "Feeder Three" are already read correctly, and the timestamps Dax quotes (02:31, 02:14, 03:06, 02:47) survive as single tokens with the authored word count intact, which is what keeps per-word cue alignment valid in that scene.

direct.note: In the room with the player. No colouring.

radio.note: A 300-3400 Hz band is the actual passband of the municipal handhelds these characters are using, and the mild compression is what a squelch circuit does. Each filter is doubled on purpose: ffmpeg's highpass/lowpass are biquads capped at 2 poles, so one stage is only about 12 dB/octave and measured a mere 3 dB of high-frequency reduction against an unfiltered take — audibly nothing. Two cascaded stages give roughly 24 dB/octave per side, measured at 6.9 dB less energy above 4 kHz than a direct take of comparable loudness, which is the point at which it stops being a subtle EQ and starts reading as a handheld. Kept to band-limiting plus gentle compression: spec 74 forbids compressing a voice until it sounds metallic. Applied before loudness measurement so the band-limiting cannot drag the measured level around.

sceneChannelOverrides.note: Delivery is a property of the scene, not of the character. Sera Holt is a voice on a channel through the prologue and is physically present later in the campaign, so her channel is set per scene rather than baked into her cast entry.

mara.direction: Structural surveyor, mid-thirties. Short, direct, occasional dry correction. Slowed and dropped slightly from Ava's default, which is bright and helpful by disposition and would make her read as pleasant. She is not pleasant; she is exact. When emotional she gets quieter and more specific, which is what the negative loudness offset is for.

sera.direction: Senior flood systems engineer, coordinating remotely. Precise, clause-heavy, operational. Left at natural pace on purpose: spec 4.2 says she becomes more specific under pressure rather than louder, so the performance must not speed up. Sonia's clipped RP reads as institutional without sounding villainous, which spec 4.2 explicitly forbids.

ivo.direction: Field clinic coordinator, running on no sleep. Conversational, human-scale, funny only when he has the energy. The slowest voice in the cast and the quietest after normalisation, because tiredness is a tempo and a level, not a tone of voice. Not the saintly doctor: Christopher's lower register keeps him plain rather than warm.

dax.direction: Local reporter and community archivist. Questions, quoted claims, names and dates. The fastest voice in the cast: spec 62 says that when he is emotional he speaks too quickly and then catches himself, and the +7% is what makes his run-on lines land as impatience rather than as a list. Eric is sharper and more nasal than the other men, so he cuts through Noor and Renna in the perimeter scene without being mixed louder.

noor.direction: Recovery contractor crew lead at Pump Station 12. Twelve years of licence and a daughter sitting her tickets on his references. Speaks in permissions and liability. Steady and unhurried — a man whose only weapon is a taped line does not raise his voice, and the near-neutral settings are the point: he is the one person in his scene who is simply doing his job correctly.

teo.direction: Depot volunteer sorting donated supplies. Young, willing, slightly too fast because he is trying to be useful. The only Irish voice in the cast, which keeps him instantly separable from the other young man in the depot without giving him an accent as a personality.

luz.direction: Field clinic nurse working under Ivo. Practical and level. Deliberately the least processed entry in the cast: she is the person who tells you the true thing plainly, and any colouring would editorialise it.

abe.direction: Night warden who never left the transit depot. The slowest and lowest voice in the cast. He has been awake for three days and is talking mostly to himself; the pace is the characterisation.

kit.direction: Teenager who refuses to leave the residential block. Maisie is the only genuinely young voice Edge offers in English, so she is reserved for the one character who must not sound like an adult. Faster and brighter than anyone else, which is what makes her refusal read as stubbornness rather than despair.

renna.direction: Pump technician working the flooded lower gallery. Speaks in hardware and refusal. The only Australian voice, chosen so she is unmistakable against Noor in the scene they share — he speaks in permissions, she speaks in guide vanes, and they must not blur when the player is looking at neither of them.

paulo.direction: Bus driver stranded at the depot since the evacuation. Slowed and slightly dropped: he has nothing to do and nowhere to be, and he has told his story to everyone already.

wen.direction: Emergency dispatch radio operator, heard far more than seen. The only cast member whose channel is radio by default rather than per scene, because she is never in the room. Slightly quick and slightly quiet — she is reading from a queue and there are other people waiting.
